+## #3403 - Guide coverage for the features shipped since v0.25.0
+
+**Decided:** extend the existing operation, setup, tool, machine and posting
+pages with the shipped behavior, the control's location, a worked example
+and the refusals a user can encounter. Keep the existing guide structure
+and illustrations. Add twelve focused release-coverage tests, and verify
+each changed guide page by restoring its upstream text and checking that
+its pin fails before restoring the updated page.
+
+**Why:** the next cut builds its guide from the tagged tree. Its guide must
+describe the controls and behavior that tree ships. In particular, the old
+Router description, Deburr width explanation and missing adaptive fallback
+warning would mislead a user. Existing pages already place each subject in
+the job workflow, so separate release-specific pages would split the
+instructions users need together. No runtime UI changes need new
+screenshots in this documentation change.
+
+**Sources:** CamCraft's own implementation, tests and decision records for
+PRs #3151, #2822, #3220, #3057, #3158, #3279, #3280, #3307, #3386, #3232,
+#3108 and #3113. These supply the shipped controls, defaults, numerical
+examples, format migration and refusal behavior. No vendor prose is copied.
+
+**Dropped:** product changes, new guide pages, new screenshots, edits to
+release files and external vendor prose. They do not resolve the missing
+guide coverage. Whole-paragraph snapshots would make harmless wording
+changes fail, so the tests instead check the documented facts and remedies.
+
+**Cost to change later:** update the affected guide section and its focused
+coverage test when a control or behavior changes. The guide structure and
+product code need no migration for these edits.

+### Fanuc AI contour control
+
+With **Fanuc** selected, open the Post options' **Smoothing** group.
+**AI contour control (G05.1)** is off by default. Enable it only if the
+control has that option. **AI contour control level** supplies the R
+value, from 1 to 10 (default 5); it is the controller's machining
+condition level, not a tolerance in mm.
+
+For example, enabling it at level 5 writes `G05.1 Q1 R5` after the
+operation preamble. `G05.1 Q0` cancels it at the operation's end and
+before a canned cycle. Probe sections do not enable it. A level outside
+1–10 is refused by name; the standalone post also reports "G05.1 Q1
+takes R1 to R10; not written" and emits no enable word.
+
+This option owns the AI contour words when enabled. It does not also
+write the operation's tolerance-based Smoothing request. With the option
+off, that request alone gives "SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN - G5.1 STATES NO
+TOLERANCE". Check the control's level settings and prove out the program.
+
+### Fanuc Manual Guide i blank
+
+In the Fanuc Post options' **Header & comments** group, **Manual Guide i
+blank (G1902 / G1900)** is off by default. Enable it only on a control
+with Manual Guide i. It writes the setup's supported stock blank once,
+after the unit selection and before the first operation.
+
+A machine-aligned box uses `G1902`: B, D and H are its X, Y and Z sizes;
+I, J and K locate the work origin from its minimum corner. For example,
+a 100 × 60 × 20 mm box with the work origin at the centre of its top
+writes `G1902 B100. D60. H20. I50. J30. K20.`. A Z-axis cylinder whose
+axis passes through the work origin uses `G1900`: D is diameter, L is
+length, and K is the positive-Z end face's distance from the work origin.
+
+Unsupported stock produces a `NO BLANK BLOCK` comment with its reason,
+and posting continues without a blank block. Examples include stock from
+a model or previous setup, rotated stock or WCS, X/Y-axis cylinders and
+a Z cylinder whose axis is off the work origin. Correct the stock or
+define the blank at the control; CamCraft does not substitute a box.
+

+On **Geometry > Boundary > Tool**, **Inside boundary offset** moves the
+picked edge or face loop before tool containment: a positive value grows
+the area outward and a negative value shrinks it. **Outside boundary

+**Rest machining** on **Passes** lets a smaller tool cut what earlier
+roughing left. Enable it, choose **Rest stock from > Previous operations**,
+then **Apply**. CamCraft reads the stock left by earlier operations of this
+setup at every cut depth; it hides the entered previous-tool dimensions.
+**Rest allowance** grows the rest area to overlap the earlier cut.
+For example, rough a pocket with a 12 mm cutter, then place a 6 mm Pocket
+after it to clear the remaining corners. Generate the program in order.
+If earlier operations cleared nothing at those depths, the whole pocket
+is cut; if nothing remains, generation reports "no rest material".

+Rest supports Waterline, Offset rings and Zigzag; Auto uses Waterline.
+The old Pocket Adaptive strategy is refused. Missing or stale earlier
+toolpaths are refused by name: "generate the program in order" or
+"regenerate the program in order". An earlier suppressed operation with
+a recorded cut also refuses; unsuppress it or choose **Entered tool**,
+which trusts the dimensions you type instead of reading previous cuts.
+Previous-operations rest is refused on a tilted Pocket; clear the tilt or

-The depth is not set: the tip stands width / tan(half the cone angle)
-below the edge, so the tool's own cone angle decides it. The window is the
-pair of planes the tip rides between; an edge running outside it is
-clipped along its own line, not dropped whole.
+On **Geometry**, **Constant width** holds the chamfer's **chord width**
+across the edge. **Constant depth** holds the perpendicular depth from
+the original edge to the chamfer face. Neither is a direct tool-tip Z
+offset: CamCraft finds the cone's contacts with both adjoining faces.
+An open rim uses an orthogonal virtual second face. A face without a
+valid cone contact is refused rather than assigned an approximate cut.
+
+For example, a 0.5 mm chord on a 90-degree edge has a perpendicular
+break depth of 0.25 mm. Set **Number of passes** to 2 to approach that
+break in two equal size steps, from shallow to full size. Each pass
+retracts to clearance before entering again. **Constant width** skips
+wedges sharper than 30 degrees; **Constant depth** skips wedges flatter
+than 150 degrees. The path notes report these skipped edges.
+
+The **Window Top Z / Window Bottom Z** planes limit the tool tip, not
+the edge itself. An edge running outside the window is clipped along its
+own line. Every pass must fit: "a pass leaves the tip window" means widen
+the window or use fewer passes. **Round** remains unavailable with a
+sharp-cone chamfer mill: "a Round break profile needs a ball-tipped
+cutter"; choose **Chamfer**.
+
+**Breaking file change:** project format version 76 stores the new break
+sizing. Loading a version 75 or earlier Deburr multiplies its old width
+by sqrt(2), converting the old setback to chord width on a 90-degree
+edge, and selects one Constant width Chamfer pass. For example, an old
+0.5 mm width becomes about 0.7071 mm. Older builds cannot read the newer
+project format; keep an older copy if needed and regenerate the Deburr
+to check its actual face contacts before posting.

+## Cutting data for wood and plastics
+
+On an operation's **Feeds** tab, open **Cutting data** and select
+**Workpiece material**. The choices include **Softwood**, **Hardwood**,
+**MDF**, **Plywood**, **Acrylic (PMMA)** and **HDPE**. State the tool's
+**Tool material** and **Flutes** too. The suggestion shows cutting speed,
+chip load, spindle rpm and feed. **Apply suggestion** writes the spindle
+and feed as one undoable change; first apply or revert any other edits
+on the operation page.
+
+For example, for a plywood pocket with a carbide end mill, select
+Plywood, Carbide and the cutter's actual flute count. Read the suggested
+rpm and feed and any machine-limit notes before applying. The router
+material tables use the cutter diameter to choose chip load. A spindle
+limit changes the suggested rpm and recomputes feed at that rpm to keep
+the chip load; the readout says when it does so. These are starting
+suggestions: check them against the cutter and machine specifications.
+
+A missing material, tool material or flute count produces **No
+suggestion** with the reason. Supply the named input; CamCraft does not
+guess it. The tool editor's **Cutting data** group also has **Add material
+row** for storing your own rpm and feed for each material. **Apply** saves
+those rows. A repeated material or a non-positive rpm or feed is refused
+by the tool's name. Rows and the material choice travel with the project.

+"""Provenance: User-guide coverage for the shipped features listed in #3403."""
+
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import unittest
+
+
+GUIDE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "content/guide"
+
+
+def page(path):
+    return " ".join((GUIDE / path).read_text().lower().split())
+
+
+def section(path, heading):
+    source = (GUIDE / path).read_text()
+    parts = re.split(r"^## (.+)$", source, flags=re.M)
+    sections = dict(zip(parts[1::2], parts[2::2]))
+    return " ".join(sections[heading].lower().split())
+
+
+class Release026Guide(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_v_carve_explains_medial_axis_and_width_depth_example(self):
+        text = section("operations/operations-2d.md", "V-Carve")
+        self.assertIn("medial axis", text)
+        self.assertIn("width", text)
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"(example|for a|for example).*[0-9].*mm")
+        self.assertIn("bottom z", text)
+
+    def test_pocket_rest_machining_uses_previous_operations(self):
+        text = section("operations/operations-2d.md", "2D Pocket")
+        self.assertIn("rest", text)
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"(previous|earlier|preceding) operations")
+        self.assertIn("passes", text)
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"(smaller|small) (tool|cutter)")
+
+    def test_deburr_documents_chord_depth_passes_and_breaking_change(self):
+        text = section("operations/operations-3d.md", "Deburr")
+        for fact in ("chord", "constant depth", "pass", "breaking", "geometry"):
+            with self.subTest(fact=fact):
+                self.assertIn(fact, text)
+        self.assertNotIn("the depth is not set", text)
+        self.assertNotIn("it has no passes or lead in / lead out tab", text)
+
+    def test_dxf_placement_has_stock_page_drop_and_unit_refusal(self):
+        text = section("set-up/setups.md", "Place a DXF profile")
+        for fact in ("stock", "drop", "import", "units", "refus"):
+            with self.subTest(fact=fact):
+                self.assertIn(fact, text)
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"(stock (page|tab)|\*\*stock\*\* (page|tab))")
+        self.assertIn("generation from", page("operations/operations-2d.md"))
+
+    def test_cutting_data_names_nonmetal_materials_and_control(self):
+        text = page("set-up/tools.md")
+        for fact in ("wood", "mdf", "plywood", "acrylic", "hdpe", "cutting data"):
+            with self.subTest(fact=fact):
+                self.assertIn(fact, text)
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"(material|workpiece)")
+
+    def test_router_kind_exposes_milling_options(self):
+        text = section("check-and-post/machines.md", "Router")
+        self.assertNotIn("no separate router kind", text)
+        self.assertIn("router", text)
+        self.assertIn("milling", text)
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"(tab|page)")
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"(option|spoilboard|vacuum)")
+
+    def test_fanuc_ai_contour_has_enable_accuracy_and_cancel(self):
+        text = page("check-and-post/posting.md")
+        for fact in ("fanuc", "ai contour", "g05.1", "q1", "q0"):
+            with self.subTest(fact=fact):
+                self.assertIn(fact, text)
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"(accuracy|r[0-9]|r value|r-value)")
+
+    def test_fanuc_manual_guide_blank_has_words_and_limits(self):
+        text = page("check-and-post/posting.md")
+        for fact in ("manual guide", "g1902", "g1900", "stock"):
+            with self.subTest(fact=fact):
+                self.assertIn(fact, text)
+        self.assertRegex(text, r"(refus|unsupported|only)")

+    def test_boundary_offsets_are_named_separately(self):
+        text = page("operations/operations-2d.md")
+        self.assertIn("inside boundary offset", text)
+        self.assertIn("outside boundary offset", text)

+    def test_wire_sharp_inside_corner_option_is_off_by_default(self):

+        self.assertIn("geometry", text)

+    def test_3d_adaptive_fallback_is_a_visible_warning(self):

+    def test_circular_returns_to_clearance_between_rings(self):
